title: Hobak Bokkeum Stir-Fried Zucchini
shortDescription: Korean zucchini is salted briefly, then stir-fried with garlic, scallion, salted shrimp, and sesame until just tender.
culturalContext: Hobak bokkeum is a Korean stir-fried summer-squash banchan often made with aehobak. Seasoning may use salt, salted shrimp, or other savory elements; cut and texture vary.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

ingredients.preparation: washed; halved lengthwise and sliced 6 mm / 1/4 inch

instructions.heading: Wash and cut
instructions.action: Rinse the zucchini and scallion under cool running water, dry, and cut on a clean board.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Produce is clean, dry, and evenly cut.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep clean produce away from raw-meat and seafood tools.

instructions.heading: Salt briefly
instructions.action: Toss zucchini with salt in a colander and rest 5 minutes, then blot released moisture without rinsing.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Slices bend slightly but remain firm.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a clean colander and towels.

instructions.heading: Check the seasoning
instructions.action: Read the saeujeot label for shellfish and other allergens, then finely chop with a clean utensil.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The exact allergen statement is known.
instructions.safetyNote: Saeujeot contains shellfish; use salt instead only as a documented adaptation.

instructions.heading: Start the stir-fry
instructions.action: Heat oil over medium-high, add zucchini, and stir-fry until bright and beginning to soften.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Edges turn translucent while centers remain firm.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep the skillet handle turned inward.

instructions.heading: Season and finish
instructions.action: Add garlic, saeujeot, and scallion; stir-fry until just tender, then remove from heat and add sesame oil and seeds.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Zucchini is tender-crisp, not watery or mushy.
instructions.safetyNote: Cook fermented shrimp seasoning through the hot dish and avoid splatter.

instructions.heading: Serve or chill
instructions.action: Transfer to a clean dish, rest 5 minutes, and serve warm or cool.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Slices remain intact with little liquid.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this banchan is stir-fried on the stovetop.
visualDonenessCues: Little liquid collects in the pan
foodSafetyNotes: Wash produce under cool running water.
Verify shellfish and other allergens on the saeujeot label.
Refrigerate within 2 hours at or below 40°F / 4°C.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains shellfish and sesame; verify the saeujeot label and prevent cross-contact.

substitutions: For a shellfish-free adaptation, omit saeujeot and season with salt only after test cooking.
Standard zucchini may replace aehobak, but moisture and timing require retesting.
ingredientSourcing: Choose firm, glossy Korean zucchini without soft spots.
Buy refrigerated saeujeot in a sealed labeled container and follow its storage direction.
makeAhead: Best cooked close to serving; vegetables may be cut a few hours ahead and refrigerated.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered shallow container within 2 hours and use within 4 days pending food-safety approval.
reheating: Reheat gently until steaming or serve properly refrigerated portions cool.
leftovers: Use properly refrigerated leftovers within the approved window.
servingSuggestions: Serve with rice and grilled meats or fish.

faq.question: What is aehobak?
faq.answer: It is a Korean summer squash often used for this dish; standard zucchini behaves somewhat differently.

faq.question: Can I omit saeujeot?
faq.answer: Yes for a documented shellfish-free adaptation, but salt balance requires test cooking.
